article.headline: Manchester United Overcomes Two-Goal Deficit to Clinch Thrilling 3-2 Champions League Victory
article.summary: Manchester United completed a dramatic second-half comeback to defeat Roma 3-2 at Old Trafford in the Champions League.
article.body:
The atmosphere inside Old Trafford shifted from a cathedral of distrust to pure celebration as Manchester United clawed back from a two-goal deficit. The 3-2 victory marked a turning point for interim coach Michael Carrick, ending a nine-game winless streak that had spanned nearly eight weeks. While the stadium was filled with protests against ownership, including tennis balls thrown onto the pitch and green and yellow balloons at the Stretford End, the players managed to separate themselves from the surrounding tension to secure a vital result.

This victory provides immediate relief for Carrick, though his long-term future remains uncertain. The club has faced numerous false peaks over the last 13 years, leading to skepticism about whether this result signals a lasting change or merely a temporary reprieve. Systemic issues remain outside of the technical area, and experts note that repeating such second-half performances on a weekly basis will require significant adjustments beyond the manager's current influence.

The match featured a return for academy product Kobbie Mainoo, who started in midfield despite spending the previous month sidelined by injury. Early in the game, United’s backline struggled, with a mistake near the halfway line allowing Marten de Roon to set up Matías Soulé for the opening goal. However, the team rallied in the second half, delivering a performance described by observers as a discrete brilliance that briefly silenced the ongoing psychodrama at the club.

Looking ahead, Manchester United faces a test against Aston Villa this Sunday. The performance in that fixture will likely determine if the momentum from this European comeback can be sustained or if the club will continue its pattern of inconsistent form.

article.headline: Andoni Iraola hands five changes to Liverpool line-up for Fenerbahce clash
article.summary: Liverpool faces Fenerbahce in Istanbul tonight for a UEFA Champions League league-phase fixture.
article.body:
Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas enter the Liverpool starting defence for tonight's match in Istanbul as manager Andoni Iraola looks to maintain momentum. The squad shake-up also includes starts for Victor Munoz, Rio Ngumoha, and Dominik Szoboszlai. These selections mark five changes to the line-up as the club continues its Champions League campaign following previous victories against LASK and Villarreal. Alisson starts in goal, anchored by a defensive unit featuring Gomez, Van Dijk, Jacquet, and Tsimikas, while the attacking options include Barcola, Nyoni, and Ngumoha.

This rotation strategy remains a primary focus for Iraola, particularly with an intense schedule that saw the Reds play Arsenal last Sunday and travel to face Crystal Palace this coming weekend. Managing squad fatigue has become critical for the coaching staff given the growing injury list at Anfield. The current unavailable list includes Ryan Gravenberch, Jeremie Frimping, Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni, and Hugo Ekitike, forcing the manager to rely on squad depth to keep available players fresh through the fixture list.

Liverpool has confirmed the bench will consist of Mamardashvili, Woodman, Kerkez, Wirtz, Isak, Gakpo, Araujo, Chambers, McConnell, Koumas, and Danns. These substitutes will be ready to contribute if required during the game. Fans can track the developments from Istanbul through live text commentary and match statistics, or follow the event via the club’s provided free audio commentary in the official Match Centre. The tactical decisions made during this match are expected to be pivotal for Liverpool’s standing in the league phase of the tournament, especially as the team looks to balance European commitments with their domestic schedule.

article.headline: Real Madrid Storms Greece Seeking Seventh Straight Win Against Struggling AEK Athens
article.summary: Real Madrid faces AEK Athens at the ALLWYN Arena this Wednesday, aiming to maintain their flawless Champions League record.
article.body:
AEK Athens goalkeeper Alberto Brignoli has conceded 13 goals in his last five appearances, a defensive vulnerability that Real Madrid’s high-scoring attack will look to exploit in Wednesday’s Champions League fixture. While the Greek side aims to improve upon a 5–1 European defeat against Manchester City, the visiting Spanish giants arrive with a streak of six consecutive victories across all competitions.

This match carries significant weight for Real Madrid’s ambition to secure a top-eight finish in the league phase. Maintaining a perfect European record is essential for the team as they look to capitalize on their recent momentum, including a high-profile win in the Clásico. For AEK Athens, a positive result against the reigning favorites would stand as a major achievement, especially given their difficult recent domestic form and loss to Panathinaikos.

Real Madrid manager José Mourinho will be without club captain Federico Valverde, who traveled to Greece but is unlikely to be risked due to a hamstring injury. Eder Militao makes his first start since returning from a long-term injury, bolstering a defense that faces an AEK squad led by Jović, a former Madrid player who struggled to find the net during his time in Spain. Stand-in goalkeeper Brignoli remains the focus of the home defense as Thomas Strakosha is sidelined with a wrist injury.

Following this encounter, Real Madrid will look to sustain their offensive average of 3.4 goals per game as they continue their European campaign. The match kicks off at 18:45 CET, marking the latest test for the Spanish side as they pursue continued dominance in the tournament.

article.headline: Power outage at London studio forces ITV to pull live morning shows
article.summary: ITV cancelled live broadcasts of Lorraine, This Morning, and Loose Women on Wednesday, November 4, following an overnight power cut at the Covent Garden studio.
article.body:
A power outage at the H Club Studio in Covent Garden disrupted ITV’s morning broadcasting schedule on Wednesday, November 4, forcing the network to scrap live episodes of several popular daytime shows. Presenter Lorraine Kelly, who was on her way to work when the issue became apparent, confirmed via social media that her program would not air, stating, “There’s been a little bit of a hoo-ha. There’s a power outage at the studio.”

The sudden removal of these programs impacts thousands of daily viewers who rely on the network's established morning lineup. While ITV initially hoped to resume normal operations following technician repairs, the studio’s power issues led to a total cancellation of live content for the morning and midday slots. The network aired a clip-based episode of This Morning and replaced Loose Women with a program titled Tipping Point: Best Ever Finals to fill the gaps in the schedule.

According to The Independent and Manchester Evening News, the network confirmed that the failure occurred in the wider area surrounding their London studio. While Lorraine and This Morning typically share the space, the outage was severe enough to prevent the production of live content entirely. Good Morning Britain remained on air, with the network extending that show's duration to bridge the initial gap in the morning slot.

ITV expects to restore normal programming beginning at 2pm on Wednesday, following the scheduled ITV Lunchtime News at 1pm. Staff intend to reschedule guest appearances, including a planned segment with musician Sharleen Spiteri, for future dates once technical operations are fully restored.

article.headline: Virat Kohli Smashes Cricket History With 13,000 ODI Runs at No. 3
article.summary: Virat Kohli became the first batter to reach 13,000 ODI runs at the number three position during the opening match of India's tour of New Zealand.
article.body:
Virat Kohli reached the historic 13,000-run milestone at the number three position by scoring 12 runs off his 13th ball in Auckland. This achievement came during the seventh over of India's chase against New Zealand in the first of five one-day cricket internationals at Eden Park. Kohli reached the mark in 251 innings, holding an average well above 60 at the position while securing 48 centuries and nearly 70 half-centuries in his career at that spot. 

This performance solidifies Kohli’s standing as an all-time great, as he maintains a significant lead over former Australia captain Ricky Ponting, the only other player to exceed 10,000 runs batting at number three. Kohli’s consistency remains a focal point for fans and analysts alike, with his ability to command the crease at Eden Park serving as a testament to his elite longevity in international cricket. 

The milestone occurred as India looked to chase down New Zealand’s target of 185 runs. India had dominated the first innings, bowling New Zealand out in 40.2 overs. Arshdeep Patel led the bowling attack with 4-70, while Gurnoor Brar and Anshul Kamboj added critical wickets to keep the scoring pressure high despite the short boundaries at the venue. India’s fielding also saw key contributions, including a notable one-handed catch by Kohli to dismiss Nathan Smith. 

India continues this series following a successful 3-2 victory in the recent T20 series. The team sees the return of several stars, including captain Shubman Gil, Rohit Sharma, and K.L. Rahul, as they prepare for the remaining four matches of the tour.

article.headline: Andhra Pradesh Braces for Heavy Rain as Depression Approaches Bay of Bengal
article.summary: The India Meteorological Department expects three days of moderate rain across south coastal Andhra Pradesh as a weather system develops over the Bay of Bengal.
article.body:
Residents in south coastal Andhra Pradesh should prepare for wet conditions as the India Meteorological Department reports a low-pressure area over the south Andaman Sea is poised to concentrate into a depression. While the system is currently moving west-northwest towards the coast, the Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre anticipates a high probability of cyclonic development within the next 72 to 96 hours, supported by sea surface temperatures of 29° Celsius.

The shifting weather patterns bring a heightened risk of heavy rainfall and squally conditions, directly impacting regional safety. The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority has issued a clear warning for fishermen to remain ashore, as coastal winds are expected to reach 55 kmph with gusts up to 65 kmph by November 2. These conditions follow a period of recent heavy rainfall in the region, where areas like Nagaram recorded 91.5 mm and Tanuku saw 81.2 mm of precipitation.

According to the India Meteorological Department, moderate rain is expected to hit isolated places across East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, Krishna, NTR, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu, Markapuram, Prakasam, and Nellore on Sunday and Monday. The situation is set to intensify mid-week, with heavy to very heavy rainfall forecast specifically for NTR, Krishna, Guntur, Palnadu, and Bapatla districts on November 2, followed by West Godavari, Eluru, and Prakasam on November 3. Officials remain vigilant, monitoring the system's potential for further intensification as it approaches land.

article.headline: Real Madrid reach verbal agreement to snatch Manchester United teenager JJ Gabriel
article.summary: Real Madrid expects to sign 16-year-old forward JJ Gabriel in January after the player walked out on Manchester United in September.
article.body: Sixteen-year-old JJ Gabriel has not trained with Manchester United since September, when he formally requested to leave the club and asked to be de-registered to become a free agent. While he was previously slated to potentially become the club's youngest debutant during a Carabao Cup tie against Brighton, the teenager has instead opted to train independently in Spain while finalizing his move to Real Madrid. The transfer hinges on a FIFA loophole concerning players who hold European passports, a status Gabriel qualifies for through his parents. article.headline: Kellogg’s Admits Rice Krispies Snap, Crackle and Pop is Quieter After Reformulation
article.summary: Kellogg's replaced whole rice grains with corn and rice flour in UK Rice Krispies and Coco Pops, resulting in a noticeably quieter sound.
article.body:
The iconic snap, crackle and pop, a marketing centerpiece for the cereal since the 1950s, is fading as milk no longer triggers the same reaction in the bowl. Kellogg’s spokesperson confirmed that while the sound still exists, it is now quieter and less instant than in previous versions of the product. The change follows a shift from whole rice grains to a blend of corn flour and rice flour, a move necessitated by changing weather conditions that disrupted global grain supplies. 

The impact of this modification reaches beyond the bowl’s acoustics, sparking intense debate among consumers. Fans who have consumed the breakfast staple for years report that the texture is now weird and stale, with some parents noting that their children refuse to eat the new version. Because the updated recipe now incorporates wheat gluten as a main ingredient, the cereal may no longer be suitable for shoppers with wheat allergies or celiac disease, requiring new allergen labeling in the UK.

While social media platforms like TikTok are filled with consumer complaints comparing the new formulation to the old, the company maintains that the products underwent careful assessment for taste and appearance. The company is actively monitoring consumer feedback regarding these changes. 

Consumers in North America will not experience these issues. WK Kellogg Co. confirmed that Rice Krispies sold in the United States and Canada continue to be made with real rice grains. There are no plans to alter the ingredients or recipes for these markets, and shoppers in those regions can expect the same taste as before.

news.title: A Lame-Duck Supreme Court Showdown Could Be Coming
news.og_title: A Lame-Duck Supreme Court Showdown Could Be Coming
news.og_desc:
If Democrats retake the U.S. Senate after the (ongoing) midterm elections, we should expect any number of drastic reactions from Republicans desperate to cling to power. Among them could be a last-ditch effort to extend their control of the Supreme Court by rushing a lame-duck confirmation process in November or December, should Justices Clarence Thomas and/or Samuel Alito (ages 78 and 76, respectively) see it as their last chance anytime soon to be replaced by another conservative.

As we fight to protect our democracy, we must be ready to hold the line.

There hasn’t been a lame-duck Supreme Court confirmation since the 19th century—well before the 12th Amendment standardized the congressional calendar. Such a move would no doubt be seen by the American people as a desperate and unprecedented effort to manipulate the membership of the Supreme Court by bending the rules when it suits them.

Moreover, Republicans' success could become largely irrelevant if Democrats follow through on reforming the Supreme Court after retaking power. 

Support for Supreme Court reform is higher than ever. A recent Marquette Law School poll found massive endorsements for the three most prominent reforms: 89 percent for a strict ethics code, 79 percent for term limits and 53 percent for increasing the number of justices on the bench. Such support would surely only grow in the face of Republicans blatantly attempting to lock in control before losing power.
